what_was_done: covering's stored branch now covers by the stored verdict's own head through the same _covers test as the computed one (head equality or patch-id from delivery.base); the delivery.head/patch_id consultation is gone. test_closure_used_without_records rewritten to summary()'s form with no delivery.head; the stale H1/H2 case added as test_closure_not_covered_after_a_new_commit; test_computed_overrules_closure's stored verdict now carries summary()'s head and patch_id; records' test_evidence_lookup review case updated to the same rule (the sanctioned ORDER section 4 edit).

changed_files runs git -c core.quotePath=false diff --name-only -z --no-renames and splits on NUL, so unusual paths arrive unquoted. The test stores an accented name (cafe.py, spelled from the filesystem so NFC/NFD agrees) and a name with a double quote, asserts both arrive verbatim and that no C-quoted form appears.

New records case r17-chain-broken-at-loop-one: loop 1 runs to blocked/cap over four passes and a later loop converges, expecting chain false; unit test test_chain_open_at_one_loop_keeps_covering_none asserts the computed verdict covers nothing while chain is broken. Killing both mutations verified: _chain reduced to the last loop and covering dropping the chain check each fail them.

Two records cases from r06: r18-repair-item-unaccounted, whose later-loop reviewer accounts for none of brand_new.py (expect failed/no_result with the coverage finding open), and r19-changed-range-unknown, whose changed map lacks the range (expect failed/no_result with empty lists, head empty — decision D10). Both discriminate items=[] from items=changed(...) or [].

r08-waive-after-cap redone as a real after-cap story: four passes that end blocked/cap without the waiver and converge with it, so removing the waiver from the case input fails the case. The waivers()->verdict() wiring is tested by test_waived_verdict_converges_through_the_decision, which settles finding.S-9.01 through decision_open/settle_decision and asserts the verdict and covering turn converged (verified to fail with waived=[] in _compute).

test_verdict_never_regounds_an_unmarked_finding added: an unmarked critical finding on src/module.py keeps blocking after a later commit removes the file, so a tool that re-grounds against the current worktree would unground it and fail the test. The grounded:false half stays in test_verdict_trusts_stored_mark.

One shared reader: story_unit.acs(body) skips fences (strips ``` and ~~~ openings and closings) and verdicts._story_acs delegates to it, so the tool and the unit cannot require different items. test_items_equal_unit_acs now puts '### AC-9' inside its fence and both readers must still answer ['AC-1','AC-2']; the unfenced story_unit reader fails it. Note: this edits story_unit.py, which the survey-2 plan edits in section 4 — the finding asked for exactly this.

New records case r20-walk-on-after-clean: pass 1 clean, pass 2 opens a hard finding with no fix, and the last pass's verdict (failed/no_result, finding blocking) is expected. The spec row 'A loop whose records go on after a pass with nothing open' now maps to that case instead of r11-cut-off-after-fix, whose records never go on past a clean pass.

The two holdout-score rows are listed in DEFERRED_TO_G6A with a comment naming the deferral (plan step-4 verdicts.md 1), and test_spec_rows_have_cases asserts deferred rows claim no case; they no longer map to j04.

r16's records are now ordered as steps_list returns them (alphabetical by step name, fix-implementer before fix-tw), so dropping D6's method sort flips loop 1 out of converged and fails the case (verified by mutation). A third fix record fix-x-l2-p3 whose passing gate sits at another sha lands in skipped with why 'gate' (verified that removing the sha check fails the case).

public_verdict maps walled keys in dismissed to walled:<12 hex> and empties the reason (kept as an empty string because verdict.schema.json requires the member), for reviewer withdrawals and arbiter dismissals alike. The test extends test_public_verdict_hides_walled with a second rebuild whose reviewer withdraws the walled finding; the unmapped form fails it.

convergence.replay sets blocked/cap at the cap when the arbitration is already spent and findings stay open, instead of asking the fixer again and ending failed/no_result. New records case r22-cap-after-arbitration: pass 3 is settled by the arbiter and converges, pass 4 opens a new finding and the loop is capped with it (verified to fail with the branch removed).

closure-record.schema.json's verdict properties renamed commit to head and gained patch_id and rounds_used, with descriptions tying them to vsdd.state.verdicts.summary, and records/closure.md's verdict paragraph now names the summary form. The schema change is an interface note for the not-yet-built checkpoint writers; summary() and test_summary_is_valid_closure_verdict already produced these keys.

conformance.test.mjs computes the judge and loop results once (a shared promise over one harness run) and registers one test per case named by its file stem, so a failing case no longer stops a loop and hides later disagreements; node --test reports 26 tests.

Derived the second way: _compute reads the stored closure verdict's rounds_used (helper _closure_rounds_used, shared by rounds_used) and _rebuild raises the last loop 1's used to at least that count, so the arbiter falls on the same pass as the script's on a clone with no or short run records; the public rebuild signature is unchanged (stored_used defaults to 0 there). test_replay_uses_the_used_the_script_was_given stores a closure at rounds_used 1 with a disputed fix and an arbitration record and asserts the pass-2 dismissal and convergence; without the floor the loop ends failed/no_result (verified by mutation).

The rejection of P3BLD-27 is re-recorded in this file, which the findings build appends to outcomes/ORDER after step4-rules.json, so the ledger shows P3BLD-27 rejected instead of left-for-builder waiting for G3; the entry below carries it.

The shorter rule (judge the last pass only) stays rejected per plan decision D1, re-recorded after step4-rules.json so the ledger no longer shows left-for-builder for G3: the tool's verdict is the full replay built and conforming here — a claim the next reviewer did not confirm keeps its finding open and a dismissal needs the dispute and the ruling (case l10-claim-not-confirmed is one the shorter rule gets wrong).
